newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares break higher, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares break higher, dollar steady.

text.p: British and French shares broke higher after a slow start on Thursday, putting concerns over U.S. interest rates behind them for the moment, while all the dollar could muster was a small rise against the yen.
London share prices powered ahead during late morning trade in a technically driven market as traders squared their books ahead of Friday's expiry of FTSE 100 futures and options.
Leading shares were within 10 points of their all-time highs and the FTSE looked again as if it might hit 4,000 points before the end of the week, traders said.
The index, which tracks the 100 leading British shares, was up 29 points, or 0.75 percent, just after midday.
"All the activity is coming from derivatives at the moment, we're not really seeing any proper business," said one trader.
"If we go through 4,000 we could have another 200 points to run," said another. "There is too much cash waiting to go in, funds are too liquid and there is nowhere else to put the money."
One large institution confirmed on Wednesday it was holding 12.5 to 15 percent of its funds in cash and other institutions are also rumoured to be holding sizeable cash piles.
"We might break the 4,000 level but I don't think it'll hold. What people are looking for more than anything is selling opportunities but they're terrified of doing it too soon," said one trader.
Bid talk also resurfaced, pushing Zeneca up 40p to 1,583-1/2p on rumours of a merger with Germany's Bayer AG.
French stocks opened weaker, but followed London higher during the late morning and stood 10 points up at midday.
Pinault-Printemps-Redoute was the top gainer on the CAC, rising more than three percent after reporting a jump in first-half profit on Wednesday.

German shares opened mostly flat and showed no inclination to move in either direction after data showing German August money supply growth came in above forecasts and a new business climate index showed confidence improving slightly.

Trading in all Europe's share markets continues to be overshadowed by U.S. interest rate concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting on September 24, which many feel may increase rates.
In the foreign exchanges, the dollar continued an easier bias during a quiet European morning session, dealers said.

Many in the market are quite bullish for a near-term dollar upturn but its failure to break higher at the end of last week disappointed and the market has been quick to take profits. "With the next Fed move certain to be up, whether it's next week or not, the dollar does have more to do on the upside," said one trader at a leading U.S. bank in London.
"But people have been stung a few times in the past when the dollar failed to perform and no one wants to take the plunge."
By 1115 gmt, the dollar was slightly firmer at 1.5097 marks and 109.37 yen.
Traders were a little surprised that stronger than expected money supply figures from Germany had very little impact.
"Nobody believes that Germany will raise interest rates as long as EMU looks fragile, so the mark must essentially be on a losing trend," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN-Amro.
"If we get strong data Germany is on a loser because nobody believes they will damage France...it all adds up to a negative mark story."
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5097 marks and 109.37 yen compared with 1.5091 marks and 109.12 yen in Europe late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 29 points at 3,984.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 9.96 points to 2,082.69.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 0.89 at 2,624.81.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $383.10 after closing in London at $383.35 on Wednesday.
